name: Neuron Arbor
desc: Neurons under the objective, the way calcium imaging or a Golgi stain shows them: each cell a soma with a nucleus, a recursively branching dendritic arbor that tapers and forks to fine spined tips, and one long axon trailing terminal boutons. The cells fire -- a wave of brightness, a back-propagating action potential and calcium transient, keeps sweeping outward from every soma along its arbor while a spike runs the axon and flashes each synaptic bouton as it passes, all on incommensurate per-cell rates so the firing never re-phases, over a faint drifting neuropil of out-of-focus background processes. Offered as GCaMP fluorescence, a sepia Golgi silver stain, electric neon, or a connectome schematic.
